extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, and contributors preparing systematic reviews of interventions (particularly Cochrane review authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, conducting, synthesizing, assessing risk of bias, reporting, and updating systematic reviews of interventions, with special applicability to Cochrane Reviews. Emphasizes methodological choices (meta-analysis, network meta-analysis, non‑randomized evidence), transparency, and use of technical advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane Reviews should answer important questions that are relevant to decision‐making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be designed with decision makers (policy makers, consumers, health professionals) in mind; scope and questions should reflect the breadth of decisions that users must make. Ensure review questions address practical, important choices between interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough planning and question construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning the review, constructing good review questions, and grouping included studies according to their populations, interventions, and outcomes for synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ahead to guide analysis stages: define clear, well‑formed review questions, pre-specify grouping strategies by population/intervention/outcome (PICO) to manage heterogeneity and multiplicity of outcomes; early planning provides support for complex syntheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate selection and use of synthesis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for meta‐analysis is supplemented by updated guidance on meta‑analysis and new statistical methods, and an all‑new chapter on alternatives to traditional meta‑analysis for synthesis of results across studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose synthesis methods that suit study designs and data (e.g., traditional meta‑analysis, alternative synthesis methods). Apply updated statistical approaches where relevant and consult the Handbook's new chapters for method selection and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of intervention complexity and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for meta‑analysis is now supplemented by new guidance on intervention complexity and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for complex interventions (multiple components, context dependence) and equity considerations when framing questions, choosing eligibility criteria, planning analyses, and interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of network meta‑analysis when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: A major new chapter addresses network meta‑analysis to support decisions among multiple intervention options, and Cochrane is actively encouraging the appropriate use of this methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When decision makers need comparisons across many interventions, consider network meta‑analysis and follow the Handbook's guidance on assumptions, model choice, and interpretation to ensure appropriate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded guidance on non‑randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance on the use of non‑randomized studies has been extensively expanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where randomized trials are unavailable or insufficient, apply the Handbook's expanded methods for identifying, appraising, and synthesizing non‑randomized evidence, following specific recommendations (see ROBINS‑I chapter) about design, confounding, and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial developments in guidance on risk of bias assessment are reflected, with an updated overview of key concepts supported by dedicated chapters on the RoB 2 tool for assessing bias in randomized trials, the ROBINS‑I tool for assessing bias in non‑randomized studies of interventions, and a new framework for considering reporting biases and bias due to missing results in a synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RoB 2 for randomized trials and ROBINS‑I for non‑randomized studies; apply the Handbook's new framework to assess reporting biases and missing results at both study and synthesis levels; follow detailed chapters for applying tools and interpreting risk assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and search a broad range of evidence sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated guidance on identifying sources of evidence includes information on sources other than published trials (such as clinical study reports), an extended technical supplement on sources to search...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search beyond journal publications (e.g., clinical study reports, registries, grey literature); consult the technical supplement for recommended sources and search strategies to reduce publication and reporting biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate technical advances (text mining, machine learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: An introduction to the role of technical advances such as text mining and machine learning is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and, where appropriate, apply automated and semi‑automated technologies (text mining, machine learning) to improve search, screening, and data‑management efficiency, following the Handbook's discussion of benefits and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt prospective and living review approaches when suitable
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective approaches such as living systematic reviews are introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rapidly evolving topics or where continual updating is valuable, consider living systematic review methods as outlined in the Handbook; plan processes for ongoing surveillance, updating, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address heterogeneity and multiplicity proactively
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning ahead will provide more support to authors at the analysis stages of the review and is of particular assistance for reviews with high levels of heterogeneity or multiplicity of outcome measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate potential heterogeneity and multiple outcomes during protocol development; prespecify subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and multiplicity strategies to avoid post‑hoc decisions and spurious findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: explain what was done and why
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever is done, reviewers should clearly explain what was done, and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, explicit methods sections and rationales for all decisions (eligibility, synthesis choices, risk of bias handling, analyses) so users can understand and appraise the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handbook guidance supplements but does not replace good judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines are not a substitute for good judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the Handbook's recommendations thoughtfully; use methodological guidance in conjunction with subject‑matter expertise and reasoned judgement when making review decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane‑specific planning, reporting, and updating requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For authors working with Cochrane, new online‑only chapters will provide guidance specific to Cochrane Reviews, covering the planning and logistics stages of Cochrane Reviews as well as guidance on reporting and updating reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cochrane authors should consult online‑only chapters for procedures and expectations unique to Cochrane (workflow, editorial processes, reporting standards, update policies) in addition to general methodological chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support author competence through training and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane provides a range of training and other guidance for authors, editors and other contributors to systematic reviews to assist them in meeting the high standards expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and contributors are encouraged to use Cochrane training resources to implement Handbook methods correctly; training supports consistent application of complex methods and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an evidence base and methodological expertise to inform methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The new Handbook draws on the expertise of over 100 contributing methodologists and editors... These international leaders conduct research to develop the evidence base that underpins the methodological guidance in the Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt methods supported by methodological research; rely on validated tools and consensus guidance developed by specialist methods groups as presented in the Handbook.
